To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the pre-equilibrium emission of dileptons is enhanced by the anisotropic expansion of the plasma and that this enhancement can be used to determine experimentally the isotropization/ thermalization time of the plasma.

(1) high-energy dilepton spectra from a quark gluon plasma that is anisotropic in momentum space are enhanced by a factor of at most 2 relative to an isotropic plasma and (2) the effect of an anisotropic plasma on the high-energy dilepton spectrum is significantly reduced if the plasma isotropizes rapidly, i.e., if the isotropization/ thermalization time is of order 2 fm/$ c$.

the anisotropy and the hard momentum scale of a quark-guon plasma can be time dependent, and that the resulting time dependence of the dilepton yield can be used to constrain the isotropization time of the plasma.

pre-equilibrium emission is a generic feature of any plasma that is not initially isotropic and that it should be taken into account in any quantitative study of dilepton production from heavy-ion collisions.
